views.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Keep the G20 90-day window open and press the live high-level talks for enforceable structural commitments on IP, forced tech transfer, and verification. Do not hike List 3 while talks are underway, and do not roll back existing Section 301 tariffs or trade Meng/Huawei charges for a purchases-only deal. Hold the March 1 10-to-25 percent hike as unused leverage.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: For the United States this is a modest opportunity, not an existential threat. Combined Section 301 coverage is already about $250B, the January 1 hike was suspended at the December 1 G20, and Lighthizer has told Congress the March 1 deadline will not be extended. January talks show purchase interest but unresolved enforcement and structural issues—the same mix that collapsed after the May 19 2018 on-hold statement. EXPCH is down about 27 percent and soy/ag is the exposed sector, but that is concentrated farm-belt pain, not a broad U.S. recession. Sentiment and industrial production have softened, yet VIX has receded and CNY has strengthened. Escalating now would likely freeze talks; conceding without enforcement would repeat May 2018. Negotiate with the clock running.
key_factors: Ag/soy export hit is real but concentrated
Huawei/Meng is a separate law-enforcement track
Existing tariff coverage already supplies leverage

sources_cited.excerpt: G20 90-day window; List 3 hike to 25% suspended.
Section 301 coverage about $250B of Chinese imports.
U.S. exports to China $7.1B in January 2019, down about 27%.
